definition: Seismology-based exploration estimates subsurface rock structure by sending sound/energy waves into the ground and analyzing the timing and strength of the echoes.
core_idea: Because different rock types transmit energy at different speeds, engineers can infer rock layer type and depth from how sound waves echo back, helping locate likely oil/gas traps before drilling.
key_points: Seismology studies how energy waves (sound, earthquakes) pass through the Earth.
Engineers generate sound waves and measure the timing/strength of the returning echo to infer rock type and depth.
Seismology is not exact — even confirming a trapped liquid exists may still require drilling a well to identify what the liquid actually is.
relationships: Used to locate oil traps, which are defined by permeability/porosity of surrounding rock
trading_implications: Exploration uncertainty (seismology is imprecise) contributes to upstream supply risk that can affect crude price volatility.
caveats: Seismology only indicates likely rock/trap structure, not confirmed presence or composition of oil — drilling is still required for certainty.
